title.narrative: Humanitarian Response to Support the most vulnerable people in areas with the highest severity of needs in Tigray region, Ethiopia.

description.narrative: ltpgtltbrgtLocation: Aduwa, Axum, and Abi Adi woredas of the Tigray region. ltbrgtDuration: 8 monthsltbrgtBudget: $400,000ltbrgtContext: These areas remain among the most vulnerable due to the impact of protracted conflict, prolonged drought, and the breakdown of essential services, resulting in widespread displacement and severe WASH-related challenges. The disruption of water supply systems, lack of sanitation facilities, and limited hygiene services have heightened the risk of waterborne disease outbreaks, particularly cholera, and have severely affected the dignity and well-being of displaced populations. In May 2025, SCI, Nexuses, and OSSA conducted a joint WASH assessment across 18 IDP camps in Axum, Adwa, and Abi Adi, covering 37,265 households (207,819 individuals), including vulnerable groups. The findings reveal severe water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) deficiencies:ltbrgt Water access is critically low—2–5 liters per person per day, below SPHERE standards—with long queues and reliance on unsafe sources. Eight camps use untreated water, leading to increased disease.ltbrgt Sanitation is severely lacking, with over 100 people per latrine in some camps and widespread open defecation.ltbrgt Hygiene conditions are dire: no soap, handwashing facilities, or menstrual hygiene support, and poor waste management.ltbrgt Health risks include outbreaks of diarrhea, bilharzia, parasites, malaria, typhus, and potential cholera.ltbrgtObjective: Save the Children (SCI) proposes a focused, coordinated, urgent WASH yet multi-sectoral response or emergency intervention aimed at delivering life-saving services and building community resilience among internally displaced populations in Aduwa, Axum, and Abi Adi woredas of the Tigray region. ltbrgtStrategies: To address these urgent needs, in partnership with NEXUS, PAD and OSSHD for complementarity, the project will rehabilitate non-functional water schemes, extend pipeline connections to 12 IDP sites, install solar-powered water systems to ensure sustainable access, and provide water treatment chemicals. In addition, the intervention includes the construction and rehabilitation of sex-segregated latrines with handwashing facilities, desludging and maintenance of waste pits, construction of solid and liquid waste disposal pits, and the rehabilitation of shower facilities and washing basins. IPC and cleaning supplies will be distributed to support infection prevention and control, particularly in IDP-hosting areas. Hygiene promotion activities will also be carried out to enhance awareness and adoption of safe hygiene behaviors. ltbrgtProject Target: This WASH intervention is expected to directly benefit approximately 12,750 people and indirectly support an additional 22,700 individuals, including community members, health workers, and traders. By restoring access to safe water and sanitation and promoting hygienic practices, the project will reduce public health risks, prevent disease outbreaks, and contribute to the overall well-being and dignity of IDPs and host communities in the targeted woredasltbrgtltbrgtlt/pgt
